text.p: - Alexander Lykashenko's embrace will stifle Russia
- A two-step heart transplant operation was successfully conducted in Russia for the third time.
- About 800,000 Russians infected with AIDS are doomed to die by the end of the century due to financial problems in the country.
- Russia's trade union leaders will demand on March 27, a nationwide day of protest action that economic reforms should be corrected.
- Helsinki summit agreements seem to have been subject to revision before Boris Yeltsin returned home.
- To maintain its influence on the post Soviet territory Russia should change its policy towards CIS counties, writes the paper on the eve CIS summit on March 28.
- Moscow is ready to establish a stratigic partnership with India and China.
- Trade Union leaders expect 100,000 poeple to participate in Moscow's part of a nationwide protest action on March 27.
- The main result of Helsinki summit is clear for everybody - United States will do anything to expand NATO, writes the paper from Belarus.
- Grigory Yavlinsky rejected a coalition with the new cabinet until Yeltsin refuses to influence economic reforms.
- The number of cases of AIDS infection has grown considerably in Russia due to the spread of drug addiction among young people.
